content:
Here’s a translation of the provided ancient Greek text into English:

"But Agamemnon, lord of men, spoke again:  
'I rejoice, Laertes' son, hearing your tale:  
for it is indeed my fate that you have heard and declared.  
But I wish to swear to these things; my heart urges me,  
and I will not swear falsely, in the presence of a divine being.  
And let Achilles remain there, although he is pressed by Ares;  
but you all, remaining, gather together, so that the gifts  
may come from the tent, and we may break our solemn oaths.  
But to you, I command and direct this:  
having drawn the best of the Achaeans together,  
bring the gifts to my ship, as many as we promised to Achilles  
to give him yesterday, and also to summon the women.  
And let Talthybius quickly prepare for me a boar,  
to sacrifice to Zeus and to Helios.'"

Note: The translation attempts to capture the meaning and tone of the original Greek text while maintaining clarity in English.
